The new parameter is optional and defaults to null (`body ?? null`), so those callers send exactly what they sent before. Nothing breaks.

No production code passes a body yet. config.service.ts:68 still calls `this._restService.sendRequest(url)`, which is a GET. If the frontend wiring is not done in a follow-up plan, the frontend and backend would disagree on that endpoint. That is a matter of complete delivery, not architecture, and no intent doc was provided to check it against. Now that RestService.post accepts a body, the main remaining reason for that bypass is that it needs a typed JSON response instead of WebReaction text. This is worth remembering if more services start sending bodies.

agent_notes: Signature change: RestService.post(url: string) became post(url: string, body?: object). The new parameter is optional, so the change is additive and source-compatible. The 4 existing production callers pass only a URL and keep the same wire behavior because body ?? null sends null, exactly as before: model-file.service.ts:61, 74, 87 and server-command.service.ts:26.

Wire format: when a body object is passed, Angular HttpClient serializes it as JSON and sets Content-Type: application/json. That matches a Bottle backend reading bottle.request.json, which the backend tests in commit fffa81a mock. The response is still requested as text and parsed by handleSuccess, so response handling is unchanged.

Edge semantics: body ?? null passes falsy-but-defined bodies like {} through unchanged and only maps undefined or null to null. That is correct. The type 'object' also accepts arrays and class instances, which is harmless here.

Test mock gap (pre-existing, not caused by this diff): tests/mocks/mock-rest.service.ts defines only sendRequest and has no post(). Once config.service.ts moves to post(), any spec that injects MockRestService and exercises ConfigService.set will throw 'post is not a function' unless the mock is extended. config.service.spec.ts is the likely candidate.

Blast radius of this diff alone: 1 method in 1 file. 13 files import it, but only 4 call sites use post(), and their behavior is unchanged. No schema, migration or performance effects. shareReplay(1) and the error handling are unchanged.

Cross-layer sequencing: the backend half of the GET-to-POST migration for config set (111-01) has already merged. This frontend diff only adds the transport capability. Until ConfigService.set uses it, the frontend and backend contracts disagree (see impact-001).
Verdict: the diff is safe and backward-compatible as written. The blocking concern is the unmigrated caller at config.service.ts:68, not this change.
